channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Teachers' Salaries Vary Significantly by Region, Almaty Region Reports Highest Pay.
item.description: Teachers' salaries in Kazakhstan show significant regional disparities, with the lowest monthly pay at 33,497 tenge and the highest reaching 1.2 million tenge in the Almaty region. Factors influencing salary include qualifications, teaching load, and additional responsibilities like class supervision.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Finance Ministry to Gain New Budgetary Control Powers
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Finance will have expanded powers in managing state funds, debt, and controlling budget expenditures. A new government resolution grants the ministry authority to develop financial instruments, assess investment project efficiency, and manage the Stabilization Fund. It will also establish a digital system for auditing state finances and reporting corruption.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes First Industrial Park in Chuy Region for Public Discussion
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy and Commerce has proposed the creation of the country's first industrial park in the Chuy region, covering over 24 hectares. The project, estimated at 1.5 billion soms, aims to attract investment, create jobs, and develop industrial infrastructure. The managing company will be state-owned, with plans to transition to self-financing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ranks Fifth Globally in Projected Economic Growth for 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is projected to rank fifth globally in economic growth for 2026, according to the International Monetary Fund's forecasts. The country's economy is expected to grow significantly, with Guyana and Taiwan leading the projected growth rates. This forecast was shared by Temir Sariev, President of the Chamber of Commerce and former Prime Minister.

item.title: Astana Police Dismantle Criminal Group Issuing Illegal Driving Licenses
item.description: Astana authorities have concluded an investigation into an organized crime group involved in the illegal issuance of driving licenses. The group, comprising Special Public Service Center employees and intermediaries, facilitated cheating on theory tests and falsifying practical exam results. 74 individuals obtained licenses fraudulently in 2025.

item.title: Oil Prices Hit Five-Month High, Raising Inflation Concerns for Kazakhstan
item.description: Oil prices have reached their highest level in five months, with Brent crude exceeding $114 per barrel, driven by escalating tensions in the Middle East. Experts predict this could increase budget revenues but also fuel global inflation, potentially raising import costs for Kazakhstan. The long-term impact on the global economy is viewed negatively.

item.title: US Reportedly Proposes Ukraine Join EU in Exchange for NATO Renunciation
item.description: The United States is reportedly proposing that Ukraine join the European Union in exchange for renouncing NATO membership, according to The Economist. The US peace plan also includes easing sanctions on Russia, partially restoring its relations with the West, and establishing a demilitarized zone in the Donetsk region.

item.title: Early Marriages in Tajikistan: UNICEF Highlights Persistent Issue and Solutions
item.description: An estimated 5,600 marriages involving girls under 18 occur annually in Tajikistan. In 2024, courts approved 3,804 requests to lower the marriage age, with 771 marriages officially registered for 17-year-old girls. UNICEF supports research highlighting the social and behavioral factors contributing to child marriages.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Minister of Culture Awards State Honors to 62 Individuals
item.description: On the eve of Republic Day, Kazakhstan's Minister of Culture and Information, Arman Kyryqbayev, presented state awards to 62 citizens for their significant contributions to culture, arts, literature, and media. The minister emphasized the importance of culture and arts in strengthening societal cohesion.

item.title: Kazakh President Emphasizes Sovereignty and Independence as Priceless Treasures
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that sovereignty and independence are the nation's most valuable treasures during a ceremony for Republic Day. He praised the older generation for their hard work and overcoming challenges, and noted the positive trend of youth respecting national history. He stressed strengthening statehood as a sacred duty.

item.title: NVIDIA Expands Partnerships in Kazakhstan to Develop AI Hub
item.description: NVIDIA is deepening its collaboration in Kazakhstan, leveraging the country's resources and talent for AI development. NVIDIA founder Jensen Huang met with President Tokayev, discussing investments in computing, robotics, and technology. Huang praised Kazakhstan's 'AI nation' declaration, and Tokayev awarded him the Order of Dostyk, First Class.

item.title: France Mobilizes 70,000 Security Forces for Anticipated Mass Protests
item.description: France is preparing for a new wave of mass protests expected on Saturday, October 24, with authorities mobilizing 70,000 police and gendarmes. This increase is in response to potential riots and follows previous demonstrations against the rising cost of living that saw clashes with police and property damage.

item.title: Kazakhstan Railway Worker Dies from Burns After Gasoline Spill Accident
item.description: A 46-year-old worker for Kazakhstan Railways (KTZ) has died from severe burns sustained during a gasoline transfer incident in the Aktobe region. The man had suffered burns to 85% of his body. Another injured worker is receiving treatment in Astana. KTZ is investigating the accident.

item.title: Trump Threatens New Military Operation Against Iran Codenamed 'Epic Fury'
item.description: US President Donald Trump stated that Washington might conduct another small military operation against Iran, codenamed 'Epic Fury,' if Tehran refuses to accept US terms. Trump emphasized that a new phase of the operation would only be necessary if Iran refuses to negotiate. He suggested that 'smart leadership' in Iran should agree to talks to avoid further strikes.

item.title: Turkmenistan Seeks Wider Gas Export Markets at Ashgabat Conference
item.description: Turkmenistan hosted an annual oil and gas conference in Ashgabat, attracting around 700 foreign participants. The event focused on increasing gas export markets, with discussions on artificial intelligence in the sector. Turkmenistan reiterated its support for the Trans-Caspian Gas Pipeline project and its readiness to supply gas, emphasizing interest in the entire Trans-Caspian corridor.

item.title: Kazakhstan's East Region Focuses on Processing Raw Agricultural Products
item.description: The East Kazakhstan region is increasing its agricultural output, with a focus on developing domestic processing of raw materials. Discussions at a parliamentary committee meeting highlighted the need to fully utilize production capacities and address financing issues. Despite growth, challenges remain regarding raw material imports and access to affordable finance, according to officials.

item.title: Alexander Bublik Credits Home Crowd Support for Quarterfinal Win at Almaty Open
item.description: Kazakhstan's top tennis player, Alexander Bublik, attributed his quarterfinal victory over Karen Khachanov at the Almaty Open to strong home crowd support. He stated the crowd's energy was particularly impactful during crucial moments of the three-set match, helping him advance to the semifinals.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Awards Internal Affairs Ministry Staff for Service
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan has awarded a group of employees from the Ministry of Internal Affairs for their long-term service, contributions to public safety, and exemplary work. Awards included the orders of 'Mehnat shuhrati', 'Mardlik', 'Do'stlik', and 'Salomatlik II degree', as well as the 'Jasorat' medal.

item.title: Uzbekistan Cracks Down on Illegal Sales of Liquefied Gas Cylinders
item.description: Over 120 cases of illegal liquefied gas cylinder circulation were detected in Uzbekistan between October 19-21. Authorities confiscated over 3,000 cylinders, totaling 13.6 tons, intended for un-gassified areas. The crackdown involved security services, the Interior Ministry, and the Prosecutor General's Office.

item.title: Eight Nations Urge Diplomatic Solution to Iran War, Reopening of Hormuz Strait
item.description: Foreign ministers from eight European and Middle Eastern countries met in Istanbul to emphasize the need to prevent escalation of the Iran war, seek a diplomatic resolution, and ensure freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. They agreed that military intervention is not a solution.

item.title: Almaty LRT Depot Construction Progressing in Industrial Zone
item.description: Construction of the Almaty Light Rail Transit (LRT) depot is underway in the Alatau district's industrial zone. The 19-hectare site will accommodate up to 50 train sets for maintenance and preparation for daily service. Earthworks are currently in progress, involving various heavy machinery. The first LRT line is slated for launch by the end of 2027.

item.title: Turkmenistan to Modernize 'Türkmengaz' State Concern's Infrastructure
item.description: Turkmenistan's President has signed a decree to modernize the material and technical base of the 'Türkmengaz' state concern. This initiative aims to successfully implement the tasks set for the oil and gas sector in the new era of the prosperous state.

item.title: Turkmenistan Approves Ashgabat-Dashoguz Highway Project and Construction
item.description: In line with the national program for socio-economic development, Turkmenistan's President has authorized the Ministry of Automobile Roads to contract the design and construction of the Ashgabat-Dashoguz highway. The project includes a 546 km highway and an 812-meter bridge.

item.title: Over 1.3 Billion Tenge Recovered for the State in Aktobe
item.description: The Aktobe city prosecutor's office identified violations causing damage to state interests during an audit of public procurement laws. Unscrupulous contractors failed to recover contract security sums and advance payments for infrastructure projects. Over 556 million tenge in budget funds were overpaid for special equipment and later returned. Over 1.3 billion tenge was recovered for the state.

item.title: Uzbekistan Presents Rich Spiritual and Scientific Heritage of Maverannahr in Geneva
item.description: An international scientific conference on the "Islamic Civilization: The Great Spiritual and Scientific Heritage of Maverannahr and Horizons of Enlightenment" was held at the UN European headquarters in Geneva. The event, organized by Uzbek institutions, showcased the rich heritage of Islamic thinkers like Imam Bukhari, Imam Termizi, and Imam Moturidi, aligning with an initiative by President Mirziyoyev.

item.title: UN Human Rights Experts Urge EU States to Avoid Deporting Afghans to Risky Conditions
item.description: UN human rights experts have cautioned European Union member states against deporting Afghan nationals. They emphasized the need for governments to assess individual risks and adhere to international laws prohibiting returns where individuals might face severe human rights violations.

item.title: US Trials New Personalized Vaccine to Reduce Skin Cancer Recurrence Risk by 42%
item.description: A new personalized vaccine designed to reduce the risk of skin cancer recurrence after surgery has been tested in the US. The vaccine, prepared individually for each patient, has shown a 42% reduction in the risk of cancer returning. Further details are available on daryo.uz.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Anti-Corruption System to Eliminate Root Causes and Serve the People
item.description: Uzbekistan is making the fight against corruption a state policy priority, aiming to eliminate its causes rather than just consequences. The goal is to transform public service into a system that serves the people and upholds the rule of law. Director of the Anti-Corruption Agency Akmal Burkhanov detailed these efforts.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Study Singapore's Water-Saving Technologies Through New Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan's Institute for Agricultural Development and Singapore's Rivulis Irrigation have signed a memorandum of cooperation to widely implement water-saving technologies. The project aims to improve farmers' knowledge of modern irrigation methods. This initiative supports Uzbekistan's goal to expand water-saving technology use to 3.5 million hectares by 2026-2028.

item.title: South Korea Proposes Military Talks with North Korea to Clarify Border and Restore Communication
item.description: South Korea has proposed military talks with North Korea to jointly clarify the border line and restore severed communication channels. The proposal aims to prevent military clashes and accidental deaths along the border. This initiative seeks to de-escalate tensions and improve inter-Korean relations through dialogue.

item.title: UAE Closes Beaches and Coastal Areas Due to Oil Spill
item.description: All beaches and coastal areas in the Umm Al Quwain emirate of the UAE have been temporarily closed due to an oil spill from a tanker. The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment reported the incident, stating cleanup operations have begun. Residents in Sharjah and Ajman reported a foul odor.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Implement Electronic Visa System for Foreign Nationals
item.description: Starting November 1, Kazakhstan will introduce the QazETA electronic visa system at Aktau airport and select vehicle checkpoints. Initially recommended until July 1, 2027, it will become mandatory thereafter. Applications must be submitted at least 72 hours before travel. The electronic visa is free and valid for 180 days. Exemptions apply to children under 16 and citizens over 65.

item.title: Turkistan Celebrates Republic Day Amidst Significant Achievements
item.description: Turkistan hosted a celebratory event for Republic Day, attended by intellectuals, veterans, and leaders from various sectors. Governor Nuralhan Kosherov highlighted the region's development, noting a threefold increase in GDP to 5.4 trillion tenge over seven years. The region leads nationally in socio-economic development indicators.

item.title: Uzbekistan Joins Artemis Accords for Space Exploration, Becoming 77th Participant
item.description: Uzbekistan joined the Artemis Accords for the exploration of the Moon, Mars, comets, and asteroids on October 19, becoming the 77th participating state. The Accords, rooted in the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, establish principles for peaceful space exploration, including that celestial bodies cannot be claimed as national territory.

item.title: First Lake Outburst Warning System Installed on Ala-Archa River in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The first lake outburst warning system in Kyrgyzstan has been installed and tested on the Ala-Archa River. Implemented as part of the UNESCO-led GLOFCA regional project, the system aims to enhance public resilience to climate change risks and aid rescue operations. The Ministry of Emergency Situations of the Kyrgyz Republic reported the completion of the work.

item.title: Uzbekistan's 'Uzvinsuvtaminot' Seeks Cooperation with US Companies for Water Infrastructure Modernization
item.description: Uzbekistan's 'Uzvinsuvtaminot' is developing cooperation with US companies to improve drinking water quality, wastewater systems, and infrastructure. A delegation met with representatives from Aquatech, Nobel Systems, and Honeywell International to discuss modernizing water facilities, digitalization, and new investment projects. Both sides expressed interest in further collaboration.

item.title: Kremlin Spokesperson Announces Trilateral Russia-Ukraine-US Security Talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov announced that trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the US will take place in Abu Dhabi. Scheduled for the first half of November, the exact date is unconfirmed. The discussions will focus on security issues for both nations post-peace settlement. Peskov did not rule out European participation but confirmed the primary format is trilateral.

item.title: Russia's Entry Ban for Migrants Increased by 76%, Over 260,000 Foreign Citizens Denied Entry
item.description: Russia's entry ban for migrants has increased by 76%, with over 260,000 foreign citizens denied entry in the first eight months of 2026. The majority of restrictions were applied to deported individuals and those who violated legislation.

item.title: Taliban Spokesperson Denies Involvement in Pakistan's Insecurity
item.description: Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid denied claims of the group's involvement in Pakistan's insecurity, stating it is neither beneficial nor within their capability. He asserted that Afghanistan would suffer from instability in neighboring Pakistan and accused Pakistani security officials of blaming the Taliban to distract from their own failures. Mujahid also alleged that Pakistan funds destabilization efforts within Afghanistan.

item.title: International Court Dismisses Kazakhstan's $12 Billion Lawsuit
item.description: The International Court has rejected Kazakhstan's lawsuit seeking $12 billion in damages. Details regarding the specific case and the court's reasoning for dismissal were not immediately available. This decision marks a setback for Kazakhstan's legal efforts in the international arena.
